correctness.rationale: The assigned analytic proof is correct at the stated one-variable Gaussian Fock normalization: A_t e_n=(1+it)^-(n+1)e_n; radializing any bounded symbol yields a holomorphic Laplace transform on Re z>0 with unique rational poles at z=-α((1+it)^k-1). Pairwise distinct powers preclude cancellation and force Re(1+it)^k≥1; the explicit bounded Gaussian symbols yield sufficiency and uniqueness follows from injectivity of the Gaussian Berezin transform. Equidistribution and finite root-of-unity counting give density 1/2 or (1+2floor((L-1)/4))/L. However the same mathematics is independently established already by a stronger earlier published dilation-sum theorem, so correctness does not imply novelty.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Earlier Oct18 theorem is strictly broader: allows arbitrary distinct finite dilation parameters and coefficients, and proves full angular algebra-closure classification, not only compact Gaussian phase polynomial powers. Lin–Lu–Zu adds a broad Fourier recognition test/single dilation but is not needed to conclude covered.

originality.rationale: FAIL on decisive implication from fully inspected October 18 2026 result 'Pole rigidity and a sharp angular subalgebra boundary for Gaussian Fock Toeplitz dilations'. In Gaussian scale α, put u=1+it and λ=u^-1. On the Fock monomial basis A_t=λ C_λ exactly. Thus for any polynomial P(A_t)=∑ c_k λ^k C_{λ^k}, and the earlier theorem's complete finite-sum criterion Re(λ^k)≥|λ|^{2k} is equivalent, after multiplication by |u|^{2k}, to Re(u^k)≥1. Its unique bounded symbol ∑ c_k λ^k (λ^k)^-1 exp[α(1-(λ^k)^-1)|z|²] is precisely the submitted ∑c_k exp[-α(u^k-1)|z|²]. The earlier paper also explicitly proves identical angular irrational and rational density formulas and stronger multiplicative-algebra boundary. The entire central finite-polynomial result is a specialization, not an original remainder; different t parametrization and proof wording do not create new results.
